about.job.text: Out here by the clamp you hear the woods talk. Wolves on the ridge last week. Something bigger the week before.
Charcoal burners see who goes through the woods by night, and who comes back. I say nothing. Mostly.
There's an old camp past the second stream. Nobody burns there now. Nobody says why.
Two days she smoulders, and I sleep beside her like a mother. Then the rake, and the sacks, and the smith pays.
The flock knows the way to the far meadow better than I do. I just keep the stragglers honest.
Up on the high grass you see everything: the road, the riders, the smoke from the burners' clearing.
The old miners left levels all the way down. We open new galleries off them, a face at a time.
Two hundred rungs down the shaft and two hundred up. You learn to count in your sleep.
Out on the water at first light, back before the bell. The fish keep better hours than people.
